Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of your requirements from the call:
- Latency SLOs: p99 target ~500ms (inference) and p95 ~120ms for interactive traffic
- Throughput: sustained ~60–80 req/s with occasional bursts to ~200 req/s
- Isolation concerns: procurement flagged "noisy neighbor" risk on shared infrastructure; they'd prefer strong isolation guarantees or dedicated options
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 evidence + standard network isolation; procurement will want an evidence pack

How Redwood maps to those needs:
- Hosted API (shared): fastest to get started, routing + autoscaling, some tenancy isolation but not absolute (shared GPUs). Good for early testing and small-scale production, but noisy-neighbor risk exists for strict SLOs.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved): reserved GPU pools for your org only, predictable throughput and stronger isolation boundaries. We can provide per-route SLOs, priority scheduling, and clearer KV-cache and memory isolation to mitigate noisy neighbors.
- Private VPC / on-prem: full customer-managed networking and isolation; recommended for very strict regulatory requirements or when you need on-prem hardware.

Questions / ask from your side:
- Can you confirm whether procurement will accept a Dedicated capacity SLA or do they require a Private VPC/on-prem deployment?
- For the workload above, would you be open to a short Dedicated capacity trial (2 weeks) so we can validate p99 latency and noisy-neighbor behaviour under your traffic patterns?

Proposed next steps:
1) If yes to trial: Marissa (cc'd) will own the technical setup and run a focused test plan. We can run a pre-trial baseline on shared and then switch to Dedicated for direct comparison.
2) We'll send the procurement pack (SOC 2, SLA excerpt) and a short statement of work for the trial.
3) Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive next week to go over isolation mechanics and test criteria.

I've attached a short SLA excerpt for dedicated capacity and a trial playbook (attachment: redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf). Link to trial playbook: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-dedicated-trial-playbook

Hi Sarah —

Looping in some technical detail so your procurement and infra teams have concrete language for the SOW. Short answers up front: Dedicated capacity provides strong isolation controls designed to eliminate noisy-neighbor impact for serving workloads; Hosted (shared) does not make that same guarantee. Below are specifics we can include in the SOW/trial doc.

Isolation mechanics (Dedicated capacity):
- Physical/topology isolation: Dedicated pools are composed of GPU nodes reserved for a single tenant (no cross-customer CUDA sharing on those nodes).
- Resource controls: We use GPU pinning + cgroups for CPU/GPU memory isolation, and we enforce per-pod device allocation so one tenant cannot oversubscribe another's GPU.
- Scheduler behaviour: Priority scheduling for reserved tenants + admission controls during contention windows; we avoid speculative co-tenancy on the same physical GPU for reserved pools.
- KV/prefix cache: Dedicated tenants get their own cache partitions (no cross-tenant cache eviction interference).
- Network & I/O: VPC-level segmentation and per-tenant egress shaping to mitigate noisy I/O patterns.

SLOs / SLA (examples we can include in procurement):
- Dedicated: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 500ms at agreed traffic profile, 99.9% uptime SLA on the endpoint; credits on breach (standard SLA language). We can scope exact numbers to your traffic profile in the SOW.
- Hosted: best-effort latency targets; not guaranteed for strict p99 under noisy workloads.

Trial plan suggestion (2-week focused test):
1) Baseline phase (2–3 days): run your workload against Hosted to measure baseline latency under your mix, and optionally inject a synthetic noisy tenant workload to simulate worst-case contention.
2) Dedicated phase (10 days): switch to Dedicated pool with identical traffic and compare p95/p99 and error rates. We'll capture token-level traces and provide dashboards.
3) Deliverables: test report, SLO verification, and config recommendations (batching/quantization profiles) for cost/latency tradeoffs.

Costing notes: Dedicated is typically a reserved commit (monthly/annual) priced higher than shared per-token but provides predictable unit economics for high-throughput workloads. For the trial we can run an evaluation instance with short-term reserved nodes; I'll have pricing options in the trial SOW.
